verses.original: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν εὑρηκέναι Ἀβραὰμ τὸν προπάτορα ἡμῶν κατὰ σάρκα
verses.transliteration: Ti oun eroumen heurēkenai Abraam ton propatora hēmōn kata sarka
verses.literal: What then shall we say that Abraham our forefather according to the flesh has discovered
verses.literalPt: Que diremos, então, ter conseguido Abraão, nosso progenitor, segundo a carne?

verses.original: εἰ γὰρ Ἀβραὰμ ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη ἔχει καύχημα ἀλλ’ οὐ πρὸς Θεόν
verses.transliteration: ei gar Abraam ex ergōn edikaiōthē echei kauchēma all’ ou pros Theon
verses.literal: If Abraham was indeed justified by works he had something to boast about but not before God
verses.literalPt: Porque, se Abraão foi justificado pelas obras, tem de que se gloriar; mas não diante de Deus.

verses.original: τί γὰρ ἡ γραφὴ λέγει Ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραὰμ τῷ Θεῷ καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην
verses.transliteration: ti gar hē graphē legei Episteusen de Abraam tō Theō kai elogisthē autō eis dikaiosynēn
verses.literal: For what does the Scripture say Abraham believed God and it was credited to him as righteousness
verses.literalPt: Pois que diz a Escritura? E Abraão creu a Deus, e isso lhe foi imputado para justiça.

verses.original: Τῷ δὲ ἐργαζομένῳ ὁ μισθὸς οὐ λογίζεται κατὰ χάριν ἀλλὰ κατὰ ὀφείλημα
verses.transliteration: Tō de ergazomenō ho misthos ou logizetai kata charin alla kata opheilēma
verses.literal: Now the wages of the worker are not credited as a gift but as an obligation
verses.literalPt: Ao que trabalha, não lhe é imputada a recompensa por graça, mas por dívida;

verses.original: τῷ δὲ μὴ ἐργαζομένῳ πιστεύοντι δὲ ἐπὶ τὸν δικαιοῦντα τὸν ἀσεβῆ λογίζεται ἡ πίστις αὐτοῦ εἰς δικαιοσύνην
verses.transliteration: tō de mē ergazomenō pisteuonti de epi ton dikaiounta ton asebē logizetai hē pistis autou eis dikaiosynēn
verses.literal: However to the one who does not work but believes in Him who justifies the ungodly his faith is credited as righteousness
verses.literalPt: porém ao que não trabalha, mas crê naquele que justifica ao ímpio, a sua fé lhe é imputada para justiça.

verses.original: καθάπερ καὶ Δαυὶδ λέγει τὸν μακαρισμὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ᾧ ὁ Θεὸς λογίζεται δικαιοσύνην χωρὶς ἔργων
verses.transliteration: kathaper kai Dauid legei ton makarismon tou anthrōpou hō ho Theos logizetai dikaiosynēn chōris ergōn
verses.literal: And David speaks likewise of the blessedness of the man to whom God credits righteousness apart from works
verses.literalPt: Do mesmo modo também Davi declara bem-aventurado o homem a quem Deus atribui justiça, sem obras,

verses.original: Μακάριοι ὧν ἀφέθησαν αἱ ἀνομίαι καὶ ὧν ἐπεκαλύφθησαν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι
verses.transliteration: Makarioi hōn aphethēsan hai anomiai kai hōn epekalyphthēsan hai hamartiai
verses.literal: Blessed are they whose lawless acts are forgiven whose sins are covered
verses.literalPt: dizendo: Bem-aventurados aqueles cujas iniquidades são perdoadas, e cujos pecados são cobertos;

verses.original: μακάριος ἀνὴρ οὗ οὐ μὴ λογίσηται Κύριος ἁμαρτίαν
verses.transliteration: makarios anēr hou ou mē logisētai Kyrios hamartian
verses.literal: Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will never count against him
verses.literalPt: Bem-aventurado o homem a quem o Senhor não imputará pecado.

verses.original: Ὁ μακαρισμὸς οὖν οὗτος ἐπὶ τὴν περιτομὴν ἢ καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν ἀκροβυστίαν λέγομεν γάρ Ἐλογίσθη τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ἡ πίστις εἰς δικαιοσύνην
verses.transliteration: Ho makarismos oun houtos epi tēn peritomēn ē kai epi tēn akrobystian legomen gar Elogisthē tō Abraam hē pistis eis dikaiosynēn
verses.literal: Is this blessing only on the circumcised or also on the uncircumcised We have been saying that Abraham’s faith was credited to him as righteousness
verses.literalPt: Vem, pois, essa bem-aventurança sobre os circuncisos ou também sobre os incircuncisos? Porque dizemos: A fé foi imputada a Abraão para justiça.

verses.original: πῶς οὖν ἐλογίσθη ἐν περιτομῇ ὄντι ἢ ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ οὐκ ἐν περιτομῇ ἀλλ’ ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ
verses.transliteration: pōs oun elogisthē en peritomē onti ē en akrobystia ouk en peritomē all’ en akrobystia
verses.literal: In what context . . . was it credited Was it after . . . his circumcision or before It was not after but before
verses.literalPt: Como, pois, lhe foi imputada? Estando na circuncisão ou na incircuncisão? Não na circuncisão, mas sim na incircuncisão;

verses.original: Καὶ σημεῖον ἔλαβεν περιτομῆς σφραγῖδα τῆς δικαιοσύνης τῆς πίστεως τῆς ἐν τῇ ἀκροβυστίᾳ εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν πατέρα πάντων τῶν πιστευόντων δι’ ἀκροβυστίας εἰς τὸ λογισθῆναι καὶ αὐτοῖς τὴν δικαιοσύνην
verses.transliteration: Kai sēmeion elaben peritomēs sphragida tēs dikaiosynēs tēs pisteōs tēs en tē akrobystia eis to einai auton patera pantōn tōn pisteuontōn di’ akrobystias eis to logisthēnai kai autois tēn dikaiosynēn
verses.literal: And he received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised So then he is the father of all who believe but are not circumcised in order that righteousness might be credited to them
verses.literalPt: e recebeu o sinal da circuncisão, selo da justiça da fé que teve quando não era circuncidado; para que fosse ele pai de todos os que creem, ainda que não sejam circuncidados, a fim de que a justiça lhes fosse imputada;

verses.original: καὶ πατέρα περιτομῆς τοῖς οὐκ ἐκ περιτομῆς μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς στοιχοῦσιν τοῖς ἴχνεσιν τῆς ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ πίστεως τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἀβραάμ
verses.transliteration: kai patera peritomēs tois ouk ek peritomēs monon alla kai tois stoichousin tois ichnesin tēs en akrobystia pisteōs tou patros hēmōn Abraam
verses.literal: And he is also the father of the circumcised who not only are circumcised but who also walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised
verses.literalPt: e fosse também pai da circuncisão para aqueles que não somente são da circuncisão, mas que também andam nas pisadas da fé que teve nosso pai Abraão antes de ser circuncidado.

verses.original: Οὐ γὰρ διὰ νόμου ἡ ἐπαγγελία τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ἢ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ τὸ κληρονόμον αὐτὸν εἶναι κόσμου ἀλλὰ διὰ δικαιοσύνης πίστεως
verses.transliteration: Ou gar dia nomou hē epangelia tō Abraam ē tō spermati autou to klēronomon auton einai kosmou alla dia dikaiosynēs pisteōs
verses.literal: For the promise to Abraham and his offspring that he would be heir of the world was not given through the law but through the righteousness that comes by faith
verses.literalPt: A promessa feita a Abraão ou à sua descendência de que seria herdeiro do mundo não foi pela Lei, mas pela justiça da fé.

verses.original: εἰ γὰρ οἱ ἐκ νόμου κληρονόμοι κεκένωται ἡ πίστις καὶ κατήργηται ἡ ἐπαγγελία
verses.transliteration: ei gar hoi ek nomou klēronomoi kekenōtai hē pistis kai katērgētai hē epangelia
verses.literal: For if those who live by the law are heirs faith is useless and the promise is worthless
verses.literalPt: Pois, se os que são da Lei são herdeiros, fica aniquilada a fé e anulada a promessa.

verses.original: ὁ γὰρ νόμος ὀργὴν κατεργάζεται οὗ δὲ οὐκ ἔστιν νόμος οὐδὲ παράβασις
verses.transliteration: ho gar nomos orgēn katergazetai hou de ouk estin nomos oude parabasis
verses.literal: because the law brings wrath And where there is no law there is no transgression
verses.literalPt: A Lei provoca ira; mas onde não há lei, não há transgressão.

verses.original: Διὰ τοῦτο ἐκ πίστεως ἵνα κατὰ χάριν εἰς τὸ εἶναι βεβαίαν τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν παντὶ τῷ σπέρματι οὐ τῷ ἐκ τοῦ νόμου μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ τῷ ἐκ πίστεως Ἀβραάμ ὅς ἐστιν πατὴρ πάντων ἡμῶν
verses.transliteration: Dia touto ek pisteōs hina kata charin eis to einai bebaian tēn epangelian panti tō spermati ou tō ek tou nomou monon alla kai tō ek pisteōs Abraam hos estin patēr pantōn hēmōn
verses.literal: Therefore the promise comes by faith so that . . . it may rest on grace and may be guaranteed to all Abraham’s offspring not only to those who are of the law but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham He is the father of us all
verses.literalPt: Por isso, procede da fé, para que seja segundo a graça, a fim de que a promessa seja firme a toda a descendência; não só à que procede da lei, mas também à que procede da fé que teve Abraão

verses.original: καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν τέθεικά σε κατέναντι οὗ ἐπίστευσεν Θεοῦ τοῦ ζωοποιοῦντος τοὺς νεκροὺς καὶ καλοῦντος τὰ μὴ ὄντα ὡς ὄντα
verses.transliteration: kathōs gegraptai hoti Patera pollōn ethnōn tetheika se katenanti hou episteusen Theou tou zōopoiountos tous nekrous kai kalountos ta mē onta hōs onta
verses.literal: As it is written I have made you a father of many nations He is our father in the presence of God in whom he believed the God who gives life to the dead and calls into being what does not yet exist
verses.literalPt: (que é pai de todos nós, como está escrito: Eu te hei constituído pai de muitas nações.), diante de Deus, a quem creu, o qual vivifica os mortos e chama as coisas que não são, como se fossem;

verses.original: ὃς παρ’ ἐλπίδα ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι ἐπίστευσεν εἰς τὸ γενέσθαι αὐτὸν πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον Οὕτως ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα σου
verses.transliteration: hos par’ elpida ep’ elpidi episteusen eis to genesthai auton patera pollōn ethnōn kata to eirēmenon Houtōs estai to sperma sou
verses.literal: Against all hope Abraham in hope believed and so - became the father of many nations just as he had been told So shall your offspring be
verses.literalPt: e, em esperança, ele creu contra a esperança, para que se tornasse pai de muitas nações, segundo o que se lhe havia dito: Assim será a tua descendência.

verses.original: καὶ μὴ ἀσθενήσας τῇ πίστει κατενόησεν τὸ ἑαυτοῦ σῶμα ἤδη νενεκρωμένον ἑκατονταετής που ὑπάρχων καὶ τὴν νέκρωσιν τῆς μήτρας Σάρρας
verses.transliteration: kai mē asthenēsas tē pistei katenoēsen to heautou sōma ēdē nenekrōmenon hekatontaetēs pou hyparchōn kai tēn nekrōsin tēs mētras Sarras
verses.literal: Without weakening in his faith he acknowledged the decrepitness of his body (since he was about a hundred years old and the lifelessness of Sarah’s womb
verses.literalPt: E, sem se enfraquecer na fé, ele considerou o seu próprio corpo já amortecido (tendo ele quase cem anos), e a velhice de Sara;

verses.original: εἰς δὲ τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐ διεκρίθη τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ ἀλλὰ ἐνεδυναμώθη τῇ πίστει δοὺς δόξαν τῷ Θεῷ
verses.transliteration: eis de tēn epangelian tou Theou ou diekrithē tē apistia alla enedynamōthē tē pistei dous doxan tō Theō
verses.literal: Yet he did not waver through disbelief in the promise of God but was strengthened in his faith and gave glory to God
verses.literalPt: contudo, à vista da promessa de Deus, não vacilou por desconfiança, mas tornou-se forte pela fé, dando glória a Deus,

verses.original: καὶ πληροφορηθεὶς ὅτι ὃ ἐπήγγελται δυνατός ἐστιν καὶ ποιῆσαι
verses.transliteration: kai plērophorētheis hoti ho epēngeltai dynatos estin kai poiēsai
verses.literal: being fully persuaded that God was able to do what He had promised
verses.literalPt: e estando plenamente convencido de que Deus é poderoso para também cumprir o que tem prometido.

verses.original: διὸ καὶ Ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην
verses.transliteration: dio kai Elogisthē autō eis dikaiosynēn
verses.literal: This is why it was credited to him as righteousness
verses.literalPt: Pelo que isso lhe foi imputado para justiça.

verses.original: Οὐκ ἐγράφη δὲ δι’ αὐτὸν μόνον ὅτι Ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Ouk egraphē de di’ auton monon hoti Elogisthē autō
verses.literal: Now the words it was credited to him were written not only for Abraham
verses.literalPt: Ora, foi escrito, não somente por causa dele, que isso lhe foi imputado,

verses.original: ἀλλὰ καὶ δι’ ἡμᾶς οἷς μέλλει λογίζεσθαι τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἐπὶ τὸν ἐγείραντα Ἰησοῦν τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν ἐκ νεκρῶν
verses.transliteration: alla kai di’ hēmas hois mellei logizesthai tois pisteuousin epi ton egeiranta Iēsoun ton Kyrion hēmōn ek nekrōn
verses.literal: but also for us to whom righteousness will be credited for us who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead
verses.literalPt: mas também por nossa causa, a quem há de ser imputado, a saber, a nós os que cremos naquele que ressuscitou dentre os mortos a Jesus, nosso Senhor,

verses.original: ὃς παρεδόθη διὰ τὰ παραπτώματα ἡμῶν καὶ ἠγέρθη διὰ τὴν δικαίωσιν ἡμῶν
verses.transliteration: hos paredothē dia ta paraptōmata hēmōn kai ēgerthē dia tēn dikaiōsin hēmōn
verses.literal: He was delivered over to death for our trespasses and was raised to life for our justification
verses.literalPt: o qual foi entregue por causa das nossas ofensas e ressuscitado por causa da nossa justificação.
